Subject: Clarifying DPA roles, subprocessors, and breach-notify timing — follow-up from 3/5 call

Hi Elena / Thomas,

Thanks again for taking time today — good conversation. Quick recap and a few asks so your legal and compliance teams have what they need for the DPA review: 

1) Roles: During the call you mentioned MedSync will be the Controller and Redwood will be the Processor for PII/PHI processed by your integration. Please confirm that understanding (we've drafted the DPA with Redwood as Processor; attached).

2) Subprocessors: I'm attaching our current subprocessor list (subprocessors_2029-02.csv). Please confirm whether any of these subprocessors are a blocker for you, or if you want us to provide additional evidence for specific vendors.

3) Breach notification timing: You asked about our standard windows. Our baseline (in DPA) is 72 hours for security incidents with reasonably available details; we can discuss tighter windows/committed SLAs for incidents involving PHI. Please confirm whether MedSync requires a contractual 24-hour initial notice for PHI events.

4) Logging & retention: What is your requirement for audit/log retention (90 days vs 180 days)? Redwood's hosted default is 180 days for system logs; short-term retention (90 days) is possible for customer audit logs with a config change and a note about cost/backup policies.

5) Data residency: You flagged a desire for US-only storage. We can accommodate tenant-level region pinning in Dedicated/Private or via our US-hosted region option (we can add a residency clause in the DPA). Please confirm which setup you prefer — fully US-only residency (contractual) or a best-effort US region.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_draft_v2.pdf; subprocessors_2029-02.csv

Next steps I suggest: legal review + redline, and if helpful we can set a 30-min follow-up with our security/infra lead to walk the team through the subprocessor and logging controls. Can you share a target date for redlines?

- Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Roles: Confirmed — MedSync will be Controller; Redwood will be Processor. Our legal team will push any language that reads like joint-controller. We prefer explicit processor language with the data categories called out.

- Subprocessors: We'll review the attached list. Two quick asks: can you provide a short description of the category of processing each subprocessor performs (e.g., logging/monitoring, analytics, performance cache)? Also please note whether any subprocessors have access to plaintext customer data (we assume most do not, but want the specifics).

- Breach notification timing: For incidents involving PHI we need an initial notification within 24 hours with the known facts and a timeline of actions. For non-PHI security incidents 72 hours is acceptable. If 24 hours for PHI requires escalation paths on your side, please outline them.

- Logging retention: Our security team prefers 90 days for audit logs, but we can consider 180 if there are constraints. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports per-customer retention settings and whether that will affect cost/backup SLAs?

- Residency: MedSync requires contractual US-only residency for this pilot (data must not persist in EU/APAC regions). If Redwood can guarantee a US-only tenancy/region, we can move forward. If not, we need to escalate to procurement for an alternate plan.

Proposal: If you can provide the subprocessor purpose matrix and confirm US-only residency + 24-hour PHI notify (contractually), we'll prioritize redlining this week.

Thanks — Elena

Marissa / Rishi — see answers below (quick technical/legal-friendly bullets you can share with MedSync):

- Subprocessor purpose matrix: attached CSV contains vendor and purpose; we will produce a short mapping doc that indicates whether each subprocessor has access to decrypted customer data. Short answer: logging and observability vendors (e.g., LogStream Inc.) receive metadata-only; cache/kv vendors may hold encrypted blobs; only a small set of infra vendors have potential access and we can mark those as "may access plaintext under narrow maintenance windows". I'll add those notes and send updated CSV by EOD.

- Breach notification (PHI): Redwood standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents. We can contractually commit to an initial notification to MedSync within 24 hours for incidents that involve PHI or HIPAA-covered info, with an escalation path to our Security Lead + CISO. Suggested DPA language: "For incidents involving Protected Health Information, Processor will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Customer an initial notification within 24 hours of detection, followed by timely updates as details become available." Legal can iterate on wording.

- Residency (US-only): For strict contractual US-only residency, we can offer either Redwood Dedicated/Private deployment or a tenant pinned to our US-hosted region with contractual residency guarantees for stored data. Hosted customers can generally be pinned to the US region; for an iron-clad guarantee we recommend Dedicated/Private (minimal cross-region replication). We'll confirm the exact technical controls (no cross-region backups) and provide proposed residency clause.

- Log retention: Default hosted retention is 180 days. We support per-customer retention settings down to 60 days for audit logs, configurable via Console or via API; reducing retention may change backup/restore SLAs and incur additional operational configuration (we should flag cost/backup impacts). For MedSync's 90-day ask, we can commit and we'll document the impact.

- Evidence / attestation: SOC 2 Type II report available via secure link (https://redwood.app/soc2-report). We can provide a copy under NDA or via our standard secure report portal.

Next steps: Marissa, if you want I can draft the 24-hour PHI notify clause and the residency wording for legal to pick up. I'll also produce the annotated subprocessor matrix by EOD.

- Aditya

Marissa / Aditya — this is helpful, thanks. Quick confirmations from our side: 

- Subprocessor matrix: OK, please send the annotated CSV showing purpose and whether subprocessors may access plaintext. That will be sufficient for our initial legal review.

- 24-hour PHI notify: MedSync accepts the proposed DPA clause you suggested; please have Legal send a tracked-change DPA with that clause and the residency language.

- Residency: We require contractual US-only residency. We are open to Hosted + tenancy pin if you can include an explicit no-cross-region replication clause. If Dedicated/Private is a cleaner fit we can evaluate cost. Please indicate reseller/pricing impact if we need Dedicated.

- Log retention: 90 days is our target. Acknowledged that there may be a backup/restore SLA note — that is acceptable if documented.

Next step: We'll expect updated DPA with tracked changes and the annotated subprocessor CSV by end of day Friday so our procurement/legal can complete review next week. Attaching our review notes (MedSync_DPA_review_notes.pdf).
